title.en: Children's rights and duties (additional, not in the textbook)
The girl who wanted to study

text.en:
Roja's neighbours wanted her to leave school and help at home. Her teacher visited and said, "Every child has a right to go to school."
Roja's parents agreed. Roja promised to attend regularly and study well.
"Rights come with duties," smiled the teacher.

Children have rights: to learn in school, to be safe from harm, to have good food and health care, and to play. The Right to Education says children from 6 to 14 must get free and compulsory education in India.
Every right comes with a duty. If we have a right to learn, we have a duty to attend school and study well. If we have a right to be safe, we must also keep others safe and not hurt anyone.
Our families and communities help children enjoy these rights, and we must respect the rights of others too.
Children have rights to learn, to be safe, to eat well and to play.
The Right to Education gives free and compulsory schooling from age six to fourteen.
Every right has a duty. The right to learn means a duty to study well.
We must respect everyone else's rights too.

problem.en: What duty goes with the right to be safe?

text.en: The right to be safe means others must not harm us.
In return we must not harm others.
So we have a duty to keep others safe too.

prompt.en: A friend says he has rights but no duties. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Every right comes with a duty to respect others' rights.

points.en: Children have rights to learn, safety, health and play.
The Right to Education covers ages 6 to 14.
Every right comes with a duty.
